needs: A memory view: stack frames pile up and unwind as recursive calls run.

brief.title: Stack frames during recursion
brief.idea: Each recursive call gets its own stack frame holding its own n; frames pile up until the base case, then unwind one by one as each call returns.

beats.say: This function computes a factorial by calling itself. Factorial of three is three times two times one.
beats.show: The function appears: if n is 1, return 1; otherwise return n times fact of n minus 1.

beats.say: To see how it runs, watch the stack, the part of memory where each call keeps its own variables.
beats.show: An empty column labelled stack appears to the right of the code.

beats.say: Calling fact of three adds a frame holding n equals three. It cannot finish: it needs fact of two.
beats.show: A frame labelled fact(3), n = 3 appears at the bottom of the stack, with an empty result slot.

beats.say: So a second frame goes on top, with its own n equals two, waiting on fact of one.
beats.show: A frame labelled fact(2), n = 2 is placed on top of the first.

beats.say: The third frame has n equals one, the base case. It returns one without calling anything.
beats.show: A frame labelled fact(1), n = 1 lands on top and its result slot fills with 1.

beats.say: The top frame is removed, and its one goes down to fact of two, which returns two times one, two.
beats.show: The fact(1) frame lifts off; the 1 drops into fact(2), whose result slot fills with 2.

beats.say: Then fact of two is removed, and fact of three returns three times two, six.
beats.show: The fact(2) frame lifts off; the 2 drops into fact(3), whose result slot fills with 6.

beats.say: The last frame is removed and the stack is empty again. The answer, six, goes back to whoever called.
beats.show: The fact(3) frame lifts off and 6 appears beside the code as the final result.

beats.say: At its deepest the stack held three frames, one for each call, each with its own n and its own place to wait.
beats.show: The tallest moment returns: three frames stacked, with n = 3, 2 and 1.

beats.say: Factorial of ten thousand would need ten thousand frames, which is how deep recursion overflows the stack.
beats.show: The stack column stretches upward past the top of its space, and a warning reads stack overflow.
